changes: No substantive changes. Checked the chronogram brahma(1)-vāha(7)-ahi(8), read right to left, as 871. This matches the catalogue. Checked NS 888+880 = 1768 CE. Expanded the notes slightly.

notes: The manuscript has two dated endings. (1) The Dakṣiṇakālī ayutākṣarī section has the chronogram 'brahmavāhāhigatavarṣe': brahma=1, vāha (the sun's horses)=7, ahi=8. Read right to left, this gives 871. The colophon names no era; the catalogue gives NS 871, about 1751 CE. The other date elements are Āṣāḍha śukla pūrṇimā, Guruvāra. The verse 'ayutārṇaṃ cākṛṣāt (!) tadā' records when the ayutākṣarī was extracted or copied, but no agent is named. (2) The Ugracaṇḍā ayutākṣarī section ends with NS 888 Āṣāḍha śukla 3, Śukravāra, about 1768 CE. This record uses that date as the main one. The 17-year gap may mean the 871 date was copied from the exemplar or belongs to the composition, not this copy. Neither colophon names a scribe, owner or any other person.
